Labels

Sigma decides what to work on by reading a small set of sdlc:* labels on GitHub issues, and writes them as work moves. This page says what each one means and who changes it.

The short version

One label says an issue is in Sigma's world (sdlc:goal). Another takes it out (sdlc:parked). Everything else is an overlay that rides alongside sdlc:goal and says why it cannot be picked yet. Two labels together, such as sdlc:goal plus sdlc:in-progress, is normal, not a mistake to clean up.

Membership: at most one

Membership decides whether an issue can be found and picked at all. An issue never carries two of these.

LabelMeaningWho writes it
sdlc:goalThe issue is in Sigma's world and eligible to be picked.Sigma when it files or promotes an issue; a person by hand.
sdlc:parkedA person's hold. The issue left Sigma's world and waits in a human review queue.Sigma when a goal needs a decision. Only a person gets it back, with /sigma-unpark; nothing automatic restores sdlc:goal.

Overlays: why it is not pickable yet

An overlay never replaces sdlc:goal. The issue stays visible to every sweep and is picked by none while the overlay is on.

LabelMeaningWho writes it, and how it clears
sdlc:in-progressSomeone is working this goal right now.Sigma on pick; removed when the goal finishes or is released.
sdlc:blockedWaiting on another issue.Sigma. Clears by itself once every issue it names has closed.
sdlc:blockingOther work waits on this issue.Derived by Sigma; comes and goes with live references.
sdlc:needs-labelThe issue declares a unit whose feature: label does not exist yet.Sigma at pick. Clears by itself once a person creates the label. See Units of work.
sdlc:needs-unitThe issue declares no unit at all, on a repository that requires one. Off unless you opt in.Sigma at pick. Clears when a unit is declared.
sdlc:needs-triageEvery classification tier was tried and none matched. Expected to be rare.Sigma. The one overlay with no self-heal: a person declares a unit and removes the label.
sdlc:designedA design write-up for the goal was confirmed by an independent review. Read only by the design gate.Goal review, only on confirmation. Never written by the design step alone.
sdlc:checkpointAn issue that stands for a fact, such as a unit's code reaching the main branch. Never picked or worked.A person adds it. It is met when the unit lands or a person closes it.

Annotations: provenance only

These never change what gets picked.

LabelMeaning
sdlc:followupA machine found this, for example in a retrospective. Permanent. It is also how Sigma counts the issues it manages, so removing it hides an issue from that count.
sdlc:dependencyThe issue began as a hand-off between areas.

A legacy label, sdlc:needs-confirmation, is written only when triage is switched off. A leftover is moved off by /sigma-promote.

Labels Sigma reads but does not define

LabelDoes Sigma read it?What it does
priority:P0 to priority:P4YesPick order: a lower number is picked first, and an issue with no priority label ranks last. With several, the most urgent counts. Sigma creates the label only when asked to attach one you have not made.
model:*NoNothing. A model:opus label does not run a goal on that model; the tier comes from the model predictor reading the goal text.
feature:<name>YesDeclares the unit an issue belongs to. Sigma attaches one but never creates one, because a typo would mint a label that outlives the unit.
anything elseNoYours. A label that already exists is never recolored or edited.
Technical detail

Sigma creates exactly ten labels itself: sdlc:goal, sdlc:parked and the eight overlays above. A board with a Status column maps onto these: Backlog and Ready carry sdlc:goal; In progress adds sdlc:in-progress; Blocked carries sdlc:blocked or sdlc:needs-label; Parked carries sdlc:parked alone; Done carries no sdlc:* label. The full model, including how drift between labels and the board is found and repaired, is in the label model.
